messages:
marta_cs: FYI — customer AcmeCorp reports their reserved pool rp-acme-001 shows ~75 GPU hours consumed between 2026-03-05T01:00Z and 2026-03-05T04:00Z, but token usage is tiny (~3k tokens). Invoice charged full commit. They want to understand why and whether SLA credits apply. :eyes:

emma_support: Thanks Marta. Can you paste the org_id and invoice id? Also did customer see any service errors or high-latency requests in that window?

marta_cs: org_acme_42, invoice INV-2026-03-05-77. Customer reports no heavy traffic — only occasional health-check pings and a single low-volume batch job at 02:15Z (~1200 tokens). They sent this curl healthcheck: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer ****\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` every 5m.

liam_billing: Noted. Common culprits: warmup instances, failed billing attribution (hourly rounding), or burst fallback onto reserved pool. I'll pull metering. Can someone run a quick metering query?

zoe_sre: I'll look at runtime events. Please check `pool_heartbeat` + `instance_start`/`instance_stop` for rp-acme-001. If warmup VM spun multiple times it can show GPU hours without token burn. Also check `burst_allocations` for that pool.

marta_cs: Liam — here's the minimal query they ran locally (they shared):
```
SELECT sum(gpu_hours) as gh, sum(tokens) as tk
FROM metering.usage
WHERE pool_id='rp-acme-001'
  AND ts >= '2026-03-05T01:00:00Z'
  AND ts <  '2026-03-05T05:00:00Z';
```
They got gh=74.8, tk=3120.

liam_billing: I ran the same against our hourly aggregates — matching numbers for gh and tokens. I also see several `warmup` flags. Query: `SELECT ts, event, instance_id FROM infra.events WHERE pool_id='rp-acme-001' AND ts BETWEEN ...` returns repeated `instance_start` for the same instance ids around 01:00Z and 03:00Z. Could be churn causing double-counted warmup hours.

zoe_sre: Pulling logs now. Preliminary: orchestrator retried placement due to a transient node OOM at 01:03Z -> instances restarted 7x in that window. Warmup policy is 10m billing granularity, and our metering currently charges any partial hour as the fraction of runtime. But if restarts caused multiple short-lived instances the sum can add up. Also seeing burst fallback at 02:10Z for ~1.2 GPU-hours (shouldn't explain 74h but contributes).

billing-bot: Invoice INV-2026-03-05-77 posted. Line-item: reserved-pool-rp-acme-001: 74.80 GPU-hours @ $4/hr = $299.20. SLA credits pending review. :money_with_wings:

emma_support: Thanks. Action items: 1) Zoe to confirm whether metering double-counted warmup due to restart loop (assign to zoe_sre). 2) Liam to run billing reconciliation and propose credit if double-counting (assign to liam_billing). 3) Marta to update customer with ETA and request any additional logs they have.

zoe_sre: Will do. Quick note — if orchestrator retries are root cause we should also check whether warmup instances are billed during preemption steps (known edge-case, ticket #INT-1423). If so we might need an adjustment.

liam_billing: If we confirm internal retry-induced churn caused the large GPU-hour sum while tokens low, we'll propose a one-time credit and mark for product to address warmup accounting. I'll draft credit amount once Zoe confirms exact double-counted hours.

marta_cs: I'll message AcmeCorp with acknowledgement and ETA ~4 business hours. Customer asked explicitly about SLA credits — I'll say we're investigating and may apply credit if internal fault.

zoe_sre: Update: reconciled instance_start events -> 68.5 GPU-hours attributable to instance churn/warmup loops, ~5.7 GPU-hours genuine workloads (matches token burn window). I'll attach event ids to the incident. Root cause likely transient node OOM in the region causing placement thrash.

liam_billing: Based on Zoe's numbers, I'm recommending a refund/credit for the 68.5 GPU-hours. I'll create credit memo CM-2026-003 and flag invoice for adjustment.

emma_support: Great — please add internal notes and link incident INT-1423. Marta, propose the credit to customer and offer postmortem when ready.

marta_cs: Will do. Thanks all. Closing loop here once credit applied. :thumbsup:
